test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Arrange the following Fundamental Rights in the order of their appearance in the Constitution:

1. Right to Freedom

2. Right to Equality

3. Right to Freedom of Religion

4. Right against Exploitation
solution:
The correct answer is __**2) 2-1-4-3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 12 to 35.
 
• The sequence of Fundamental Rights is as follows:
 
 
• Right to Equality (Articles 14-18)
 
• Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22)
 
• Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24)
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28)
 
 
 
• Option 2 correctly arranges these rights in the order of their appearance in the Constitution: 2-1-4-3.
 
• These rights collectively aim to protect individual liberties and uphold equality, non-discrimination, and freedom of conscience.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the judiciary if their rights are violated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Equality:**

 
 
• Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth (Article 15).
 
• Guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws (Article 14).
 
• Abolishes untouchability and titles except for military or academic distinctions (Articles 17-18).
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom:**
 
 
• Includes freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession (Article 19).
 
• Protects individuals from arbitrary detention (Articles 20-22).
 
 
 
• **Right against Exploitation:**
 
 
• Prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and exploitation of children (Articles 23-24).
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion:**
 
 
• Ensures freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion (Article 25).
 
• Prohibits the imposition of religious taxes and ensures the secular character of educational institutions (Articles 27-28).
